question: What will be the ending value of the UST 10Y Yield for these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 7 - Sep 18)

calls.reasoning: Random-walk anchor dominates a 9-trading-day horizon: DGS10 last printed 4.79 (Sep 1-2) with Sep 4 around 4.78-4.79 after a large payrolls beat, so the median is the current level with only a hair of upward tilt from the persistent Jul-Sep trend (4.48 -> 4.79) and post-Labor-Day supply. Reference class is 10-business-day changes in DGS10, whose median change is ~0. The window is unusually event-heavy - Aug CPI Sep 11 and an FOMC on Sep 16 with a dot plot where a hike is a near coin-flip (52-63% across the week) - which widens the distribution rather than shifting it: a hawkish hike is largely priced (modest upside), while a Waller-style hold would be the bigger surprise (downside), leaving expected drift near zero. Mild right skew reflects the level sitting at a 3-year high with an oil/Hormuz inflation impulse and a 30Y already near 5.21%; a break of 4.80 has little chart structure until 5.00. No human market number was obtainable: Kalshi lists weekly/daily 10Y-yield range contracts (KXTNOTEW/KXTNOTED) that match this resolution shape well, but the page returned HTTP 429 and no price was retrieved; Polymarket and Manifold have no candidate. So no blending was done - this is an unanchored own-model estimate. Upper bound 5.255 is +46bp, ~3 SD, requiring a hot CPI plus hawkish hike plus dots pointing higher and a supply/fiscal scare: priced at 1%. Lower bound 3.495 is -129bp in two weeks with no plausible mechanism, so no downside escape declared.

calls.reasoning: Reference class is 10-trading-day changes in DGS10; the class median is 'no change', so the prior is the current level (~4.78 on Sep 4 after payrolls; 4.79 FRED print Sep 1-2). I keep the median essentially at the random walk with a token upward nudge (4.79) reflecting the summer uptrend (+41bp since Jun 26), yields at 3-year highs on oil/Hormuz inflation risk, heavy corporate supply and deficit concerns, and today's 162k payroll beat lifting hike odds to ~59%. Offsetting that: Waller's dovish lean, consensus forecasts near 4.70 by quarter-end, and buyer interest that has repeatedly capped this range near 4.80. Dispersion is set above the quiet-summer baseline because CPI (Sep 11) and a genuinely coin-flip FOMC with dots (Sep 16) both land inside the window, so both a soft-CPI rally toward 4.6 and a hawkish-hike selloff toward 5.0 are live. No matching human market was found (Polymarket/Manifold none; Kalshi daily 10Y series returned no open contracts via API and the site rate-limited), so nothing to blend against. Mild right skew: the low tail needs a growth scare that today's jobs print argues against, while the high tail has a concrete oil-plus-hawkish-Fed mechanism.

calls.reconciliation: Three disputes mattered. (1) Anchor: settled at 4.78 - Runs 1 and 2 both cite the Sep 4 Tradeweb close 4.782%, more recent and more same-basis than Run 3's ~4.77 intraday quote. (2) Dispersion, the only material gap: Run 1 self-declares its 40-45bp two-year figure as not recomputed, while Run 3 actually computed n=494 9-day windows (SD 0.151, p10/p90 -0.16/+0.18). I take the computed number over the recalled one - but Run 3 then shrank BELOW its own unconditional base to 33bp on recent-regime compression, which is wrong for a window containing CPI plus a genuinely 50/50 policy decision, precisely the condition that generates that sample's tails. Landing at 0.38 (SD x 2.56) is above Run 3 and just below Runs 1-2, and it is where the reconciled computation puts me, not a split. (3) Whether an SEP/dot plot accompanies Sep 16 is FACTUAL and UNRESOLVED: Run 3 documents that Warsh withheld the dot plot in June 2026 and that sources conflict; no web access this run to settle it, so it stays as width rather than a decided premise - second-order, since the hike decision carries the variance either way. The July-CPI-vs-PCE figure conflict Run 3 flags is likewise unresolved and does not move the median. Drift is pure judgment with no evidence breaking the tie between momentum and the 4.80 cap; I take the random walk, which is what I would bet on. Reference class carried forward from Run 3 because it is the only one computed on the correct 9-session horizon.
